subject: Dedicated pool pressure: customer update, short-term mitigation & ask
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dani@fableai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:05:00Z
Subject: Dedicated pool pressure: customer update, short-term mitigation & ask

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for flagging the latency spikes this morning. We investigated immediately and are seeing sustained queueing on the dedicated GPU pool backing your us-east-1 capacity between ~07:40–08:30 UTC. That resulted in elevated tail latencies for a subset of your inference requests (primarily long-context GPT-style workloads).

Short summary:
- What happened: autoscaler failed to spin up a small set of warm nodes due to transient RPC throttling in our control plane, which increased request queue depth and caused headroom exhaustion for requests with >2k tokens.
- Impact: ~18% of requests experienced 3–8s additional latency during the window; throughput backpressure caused ~1.2% dropped requests that hit internal queue limits.
- Current status: we opened a manual reroute for affected traffic at 08:20 UTC and the pool is now returning to normal latency.

Immediate asks for you:
1) Can you confirm whether you were running any unusually long prompt batches between 07:30–08:15 UTC (we see concentration on the `gpt2-large` worker group)?
2) If you need, we can temporarily route all calls for model:prod-gpt-large to your fallback pool while we complete the deeper remediation.

Attached is a short timeline (timeline-ops-notes.pdf). Marissa and Naomi are on this thread for technical and billing coordination. We’ll follow up with a root-cause and a concrete credit proposal today.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is sensitive for production workloads and we’ll prioritize clarity and fast actions.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Park <dani@fableai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@fableai.com
Date: 2026-10-20T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pressure: customer update, short-term mitigation & ask

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the quick note.

We did see elevated request times on our side; several model runs were using a 6k token context for a batch job kicked off at 07:45 UTC. We throttled the job once we noticed and aborted remaining runs.

Two quick items:
- Please confirm whether rerouting to the fallback pool will preserve our model pinning/version (we can’t risk an older model variant).
- We’ll accept the temporary reroute for the next 2 hours if it keeps latency stable.

Also, please include the estimated customer credit in your follow-up — our procurement team will expect a clear line item for this impact window.

— Danielle
Head of Platform Engineering, FableAI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dani@fableai.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pressure: customer update, short-term mitigation & ask

Hi Danielle — looping in some operational detail and the short-term mitigation we just executed.

Technical note (TL;DR):
- Root symptom: control-plane RPC throttle prevented the autoscaler from observing timely node provisioning ACKs for a small warmup batch (3 nodes). The autoscaler therefore did not enter the fast-path scale-up and queueing increased.
- Why this mattered: your workload’s long-context requests consumed KV cache memory and pushed queueing thresholds earlier than normal; combined with the missed warmup, that produced headroom exhaustion.

Mitigation applied at 08:20 UTC:
- Manual reroute to fallback pool with compatible model artifact (same model hash pinned; we validated version match before enabling).
- Bumped your concurrency cap for the fallback pool by +15% for 2 hours.

Next actions we will take today:
1) Engineering follow-up: deploy a fix to retry autoscaler provisioning in the face of transient RPC throttles (ETA: 48 hours).
2) Ops follow-up: add a fast-fail to the long-request admission controller so very long-context batches won’t saturate the warmup window (ETA: 72 hours).
3) Billing: Naomi will calculate a usage credit for the affected window and propose a line-item.

Attachments: reroute-playbook.md (playbook used to validate pinned artifact & execute fallback).

If you’re comfortable with the temporary reroute, we’ll keep it for the 2-hour window and then fail back after a verification period unless you prefer we extend it.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T12:45:00Z
Subject: Internal: proposed credit and notes for FableAI incident (10/20)

Internal only — not sent to customer.

Proposed credit: 1.5 days of committed usage prorated based on the impacted hour window; preliminary calc attached (sla-credit-calculation.xlsx). Rationale: measurable latency and a small percent of dropped requests for a single committed pool.

Optional escalation items for leadership:
- Consider issuing a proactive operational report (1 pager) to the account exec; AEs prefer clear line items for credit + engineering remediation timeline.
- Recommend marking this event as "severity-2" for internal tracking due to customer production impact.

Soojin/Marissa: please advise if we should run the credit calculation against committed spend or total usage for the window (committed tends to limit outbound credit exposure).

— Naomi
VP, Revenue & Customer Finance
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dani@fableai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T18:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pressure: customer update, short-term mitigation & ask

Hi Danielle —

Thanks for confirming the 6k token job detail; that aligns with what our telemetry shows. We left the reroute in place for the 2-hour window and began the controlled failback at 10:25 UTC after verification. Post-failback checks show request latencies are consistent with pre-incident baselines.

Root cause (short): autoscaler missed a fast-path scale-up due to temporary control-plane RPC throttling; combined with unusually long-context batches this pushed the pool beyond headroom thresholds.

What we’ll deliver in the next 48–72 hours:
- Engineering patch to add aggressive retry for provisioning ACKs and improved circuit-breaker logic.
- Ops change: admission control for very long-context batched jobs to reduce warmup sensitivity.
- Billing: Naomi will send a formal credit line with invoice adjustments; tentatively 1.5 days prorated against committed usage.

Action requested: please confirm whether the proposed credit approach (prorate against committed spend) is acceptable to your procurement team; Naomi will formalize once we have confirmation.

We’ll follow up with an RCA write-up and a short 1-page operational summary for your execs. Thank you for the quick coordination and for pausing the batch so we could validate.

— Soojin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
